conditions.name: Acute upper respiratory infection
conditions.opd: Assess duration, fever, breathing, hydration, comorbidities and red flags. Most uncomplicated viral URTIs need supportive care, not antibiotics.
conditions.indoor: Admit/escalate for respiratory distress, hypoxaemia, sepsis, inability to maintain hydration, or high-risk deterioration.

conditions.name: Community-acquired pneumonia
conditions.opd: Assess vitals, SpO₂, severity, comorbidities and oral intake. Use local CAP guidance for tests, antibiotic selection and duration; give explicit return precautions.
conditions.indoor: Assess oxygenation/sepsis, investigate as appropriate, start empiric treatment per local protocol and review cultures/response for de-escalation.

conditions.name: Asthma exacerbation
conditions.opd: Assess speech, work of breathing, RR, pulse, SpO₂ and peak flow if available. Treat per current asthma guideline, reassess response, review inhaler technique and controller plan.
conditions.indoor: Escalate immediately for exhaustion, altered consciousness, silent chest, cyanosis or deteriorating oxygenation; monitor and follow the local acute asthma pathway.

conditions.name: COPD exacerbation
conditions.opd: Assess respiratory distress, SpO₂, baseline status and mimics. Use guideline-based bronchodilator/steroid/antibiotic decisions; antibiotics are not automatic for every exacerbation.
conditions.indoor: Check blood gas if respiratory failure suspected; use controlled oxygen when indicated, monitor for hypercapnia/acidosis and assess need for ventilatory support.

conditions.name: Pulmonary tuberculosis
conditions.opd: Follow national TB diagnostic algorithm; assess cough, haemoptysis, weight loss, fever, contact history and infection-control needs. Do not start an ad hoc regimen.
conditions.indoor: Assess severity, complications and infectiousness; use national TB programme pathways, microbiology/drug-susceptibility results and treatment support.

conditions.name: Dengue
conditions.opd: Assess illness day, warning signs, hydration, perfusion, urine output and comorbidities. Give return precautions and arrange illness-day-appropriate follow-up; avoid medicines that increase bleeding risk.
conditions.indoor: Admit/escalate for shock, significant bleeding, respiratory distress/fluid accumulation or severe organ involvement. Titrate fluids to physiology with repeated reassessment.

conditions.name: Acute diarrhoea / gastroenteritis
conditions.opd: Assess dehydration, blood in stool, fever, pain, duration and risk factors. Prioritize oral rehydration and nutrition; avoid routine antibiotics when not indicated.
conditions.indoor: Protocolized rehydration; monitor perfusion, urine output and electrolytes when indicated; investigate severe, bloody, persistent or high-risk presentations.

conditions.name: Urinary tract infection
conditions.opd: Distinguish lower UTI from pyelonephritis, pregnancy, obstruction and complicated infection. Culture when indicated and choose treatment using local susceptibility guidance.
conditions.indoor: Assess sepsis, obstruction, AKI and inability to take oral therapy; culture when feasible, start empiric treatment based on severity/local antibiogram and narrow to results.

conditions.name: Cellulitis / erysipelas
conditions.opd: Assess spread, systemic symptoms, abscess, diabetes and immune status. Choose antibiotic per local guidance and review if worsening or not improving.
conditions.indoor: Rapid progression, pain out of proportion, bullae, necrosis or systemic toxicity require urgent senior/surgical assessment; treat severe infection via local protocol.

conditions.name: Acute otitis media
conditions.opd: Assess otoscopy, severity, duration, age, complications and allergy. Analgesia and observation may be appropriate in selected patients; use current local antibiotic guidance.
conditions.indoor: Escalate for mastoiditis, facial palsy, meningism, severe systemic illness or complications; select inpatient therapy with ENT/microbiology input.

conditions.name: Acute pharyngitis / tonsillitis
conditions.opd: Assess airway, hydration, abscess signs and likelihood of streptococcal disease; avoid antibiotics for clearly viral illness and follow local testing/treatment guidance.
conditions.indoor: Admit/escalate for airway compromise, peritonsillar/deep-neck infection, inability to swallow fluids, sepsis or serious complications.

conditions.name: Acute sinusitis
conditions.opd: Assess duration, severe symptoms, unilateral findings and orbital/neurological red flags. Many cases are viral; use local criteria for antibiotic consideration.
conditions.indoor: Urgent hospital/ENT review for orbital swelling, visual change, severe frontal headache, meningism, focal neurological signs or sepsis.

conditions.name: Acute meningitis
conditions.opd: Suspected meningitis is not routine OPD care: arrange emergency transfer/admission immediately. Do not wait for the full classic symptom pattern.
conditions.indoor: Stabilize ABCs; obtain cultures and perform LP only when safe and without delaying time-critical treatment. Start empiric therapy promptly per current age-specific local protocol.

conditions.name: Sepsis
conditions.opd: If suspected with instability, altered mental status, poor perfusion or respiratory distress, arrange emergency assessment. Screening scores do not replace clinical judgment.
conditions.indoor: Immediate ABC assessment, monitoring, IV access, urgent senior review, appropriate cultures/lactate without delaying time-critical antimicrobials, source control and repeated reassessment.

conditions.name: Acute coronary syndrome
conditions.opd: Suspected ACS is not routine OPD treatment. Arrange emergency assessment; obtain ECG promptly if available without delaying transfer.
conditions.indoor: Activate local ACS pathway; serial ECG/troponin, risk assessment, antithrombotic and reperfusion decisions per current protocol and contraindications.

conditions.name: Heart failure exacerbation
conditions.opd: Assess dyspnoea, orthopnoea, oedema, weight change, vitals, SpO₂, medication adherence and precipitating factors. Unstable patients need emergency assessment.
conditions.indoor: Monitor oxygenation, renal function, electrolytes and fluid status; treat precipitant and congestion per current guideline; escalate for shock, severe hypoxaemia or arrhythmia.

conditions.name: Hypertension
conditions.opd: Confirm BP with correct technique/repeat measurement; assess risk, adherence, medicines and target-organ disease. Use national guideline for individualized long-term therapy.
conditions.indoor: Severe BP with acute target-organ injury is an emergency. Avoid precipitous reduction unless the specific emergency protocol indicates it.

conditions.name: Type 2 diabetes
conditions.opd: Confirm diagnosis; assess HbA1c/glucose, BP, lipids, renal function and complications. Individualize lifestyle and medication plan for comorbidity, affordability and hypoglycaemia risk.
conditions.indoor: Assess DKA/HHS, infection, dehydration, altered mental status and hypoglycaemia. Use a monitored inpatient protocol and make a safe medication/discharge plan.

conditions.name: Hypoglycaemia
conditions.opd: Check glucose immediately in symptomatic or altered patients; identify insulin/sulfonylurea use, missed meals and precipitating illness. Treat promptly per protocol and recheck.
conditions.indoor: If consciousness impaired, treat via emergency protocol and protect airway; monitor recurrence, review medication/renal function and investigate prolonged or recurrent episodes.

conditions.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis / hyperosmolar state
conditions.opd: Suspected DKA/HHS requires urgent hospital assessment, not routine OPD treatment. Check glucose, ketones, electrolytes, renal function and acid-base status.
conditions.indoor: Use a monitored institutional protocol for fluids, insulin, potassium and precipitant treatment; serially reassess glucose, electrolytes, osmolality/ketones and mental status.

conditions.name: Acute kidney injury
conditions.opd: Assess baseline/current creatinine, urine output, volume status, BP, infection/obstruction and nephrotoxic medicines. Urgent evaluation for oliguria, severe AKI or suspected complications.
conditions.indoor: Check potassium/acid-base status, fluid status and obstruction; adjust medicines and seek urgent renal support for refractory complications or fluid overload.

conditions.name: Chronic kidney disease
conditions.opd: Confirm chronicity; stage with eGFR and albuminuria; assess BP, diabetes, medicines, anaemia and cardiovascular risk. Review renal dosing and follow-up interval.
conditions.indoor: Admit for acute complications such as pulmonary oedema, dangerous electrolyte disturbance, severe acidosis or uraemic complications; coordinate nephrology care.

conditions.name: Anaemia
conditions.opd: Assess symptoms, bleeding, pregnancy, diet and chronic disease. Use CBC indices and targeted investigations; do not prescribe iron for every low Hb without considering cause.
conditions.indoor: Stabilize significant bleeding/instability. Transfusion decisions depend on symptoms, haemodynamics, comorbidity and current guidance—not Hb alone.

conditions.name: Upper GI bleeding
conditions.opd: Haematemesis, melaena, syncope or shock needs emergency referral, not routine OPD care. Assess haemodynamics, medicines and bleeding risk.
conditions.indoor: Resuscitate and risk-stratify; arrange urgent endoscopy and cause-specific treatment per institutional GI-bleed pathway; review antithrombotic medicines.

conditions.name: Dyspepsia / peptic ulcer disease
conditions.opd: Screen for bleeding, dysphagia, persistent vomiting, weight loss, anaemia and NSAID use. Consider H. pylori testing or acid suppression per local guidance.
conditions.indoor: Bleeding, suspected perforation or obstruction requires emergency hospital management, stabilization and specialist pathway.

conditions.name: Acute appendicitis
conditions.opd: Suspected appendicitis requires timely surgical assessment; assess pain progression, peritonism, fever and pregnancy differential. Avoid delaying referral for nonessential tests.
conditions.indoor: NPO as appropriate, analgesia/fluids, labs/imaging according to pathway, surgical review and antibiotics when indicated by local perioperative protocol.

conditions.name: Acute cholecystitis
conditions.opd: Assess RUQ pain, fever, jaundice, sepsis and pancreatitis/cholangitis differentials. Arrange timely hospital assessment and imaging.
conditions.indoor: Supportive care, antibiotics when indicated and early surgical review per current local pathway; urgent escalation for cholangitis, sepsis or organ dysfunction.

conditions.name: Acute pancreatitis
conditions.opd: Suspected acute pancreatitis requires hospital assessment; assess pain, vomiting, dehydration and cause (gallstones, alcohol, medicines, triglycerides).
conditions.indoor: Monitor severity and organ failure; provide protocolized fluids/analgesia/nutrition, investigate cause and avoid routine prophylactic antibiotics without indication.

conditions.name: Stroke (suspected)
conditions.opd: Sudden focal neurological deficit is time-critical: note last-known-well and activate emergency stroke transfer. Check glucose; do not delay referral.
conditions.indoor: Urgent brain imaging and stroke-team assessment; reperfusion eligibility and BP/antithrombotic decisions must follow current stroke protocol.

conditions.name: Seizure / status epilepticus
conditions.opd: Protect from injury, time the seizure, check glucose and airway/breathing. First seizure, prolonged seizure, repeated seizures without recovery or pregnancy needs emergency care.
conditions.indoor: Status epilepticus is an emergency: follow institutional seizure algorithm, secure airway/monitoring, treat reversible causes and investigate precipitant.

conditions.name: Anaphylaxis
conditions.opd: Recognize sudden airway/breathing/circulatory compromise after likely trigger; do not wait for skin signs. Activate emergency response.
conditions.indoor: Immediate intramuscular adrenaline/epinephrine and ABC support according to local protocol; monitor, prepare for escalation and arrange observation/follow-up.

conditions.name: Acute asthma in children
conditions.opd: Assess age-appropriate work of breathing, speech/feeding, SpO₂, hydration and prior severe attacks. Follow current paediatric asthma pathway.
conditions.indoor: Urgent escalation for exhaustion, cyanosis, altered consciousness, silent chest or poor response; use age/weight-specific protocol and reassess frequently.

conditions.name: Childhood pneumonia
conditions.opd: Assess age, respiratory rate/work, SpO₂, feeding, hydration, danger signs and malnutrition. Use current Bangladesh/WHO age-specific algorithm.
conditions.indoor: Admit for danger signs, hypoxaemia, severe respiratory distress, inability to feed or complications; choose treatment by age, severity and current guideline.

conditions.name: Otitis externa
conditions.opd: Assess ear canal, pain, discharge, diabetes/immunosuppression and tympanic membrane when visible. Avoid unneeded systemic antibiotics; choose local treatment per guideline.
conditions.indoor: Urgent specialist review for systemic illness, spread, cranial neuropathy, severe pain in high-risk patient or suspected invasive disease.

conditions.name: Scabies
conditions.opd: Look for typical itch/distribution and household clustering; consider mimics. Treat patient and close contacts simultaneously using locally available guideline-recommended therapy; provide laundering/contact advice.
conditions.indoor: Consider admission/specialist input for crusted scabies, severe secondary infection, immunocompromise or outbreak-control needs.

conditions.name: Eczema / atopic dermatitis
conditions.opd: Assess severity, infection, triggers, sleep impact and prior treatment. Use emollients and site/severity-appropriate anti-inflammatory therapy per current guideline.
conditions.indoor: Escalate for widespread severe disease, eczema herpeticum, systemic infection or failure of appropriate treatment; refer when diagnosis is uncertain or severe/refractory.

conditions.name: Osteoarthritis
conditions.opd: Assess pain/function, red flags, trauma, inflammatory features and alternative diagnoses. Prioritize education, exercise/physiotherapy and weight management where relevant.
conditions.indoor: Urgent evaluation for hot swollen joint with fever, acute inability to bear weight after injury, neurovascular compromise or suspected fracture/infection.

conditions.name: Low back pain
conditions.opd: Screen for cauda equina, progressive neurological deficit, cancer/infection/fracture risks and systemic illness. Encourage appropriate activity when no red flags.
conditions.indoor: Emergency MRI/specialist assessment for suspected cauda equina or serious pathology; treat cause-specific disease and avoid routine imaging in uncomplicated cases.

conditions.name: Fracture / acute limb injury
conditions.opd: Assess mechanism, open wound, deformity, skin, distal pulses, capillary refill, sensation and motor function; document neurovascular status before/after splinting.
conditions.indoor: Open fracture, compartment syndrome, vascular compromise, dislocation or threatened skin needs urgent orthopaedic care; analgesia, immobilization, imaging and antibiotics/tetanus per trauma protocol.

conditions.name: Deep vein thrombosis / pulmonary embolism
conditions.opd: Assess clinical probability and red flags; use validated pathway for D-dimer/imaging rather than symptoms alone. Suspected PE with instability is an emergency.
conditions.indoor: Urgent imaging/anticoagulation decisions per protocol, considering bleeding risk, renal function, pregnancy and haemodynamic status.

conditions.name: Pregnancy with vaginal bleeding
conditions.opd: Assess gestational age, pain, bleeding amount, syncope and haemodynamic stability; urgent referral if pregnancy-related bleeding is significant or ectopic pregnancy possible.
conditions.indoor: Stabilize ABCs, determine pregnancy location/viability and manage ectopic/miscarriage/late-pregnancy bleeding using obstetric emergency protocol.

conditions.name: Pre-eclampsia / eclampsia
conditions.opd: Pregnancy/postpartum hypertension with headache, visual symptoms, epigastric pain or seizure is an emergency; arrange immediate obstetric assessment.
conditions.indoor: Maternal stabilization, seizure/BP management, labs and fetal assessment according to obstetric protocol; definitive timing of delivery is specialist-led.

conditions.name: Postpartum haemorrhage
conditions.opd: Heavy bleeding after birth is an emergency. Call for help, assess ABCs, uterine tone, placenta, trauma and shock.
conditions.indoor: Activate PPH protocol immediately: resuscitation, uterine massage/uterotonics and cause-specific interventions; monitor blood loss/coagulation and escalate to surgery/transfusion when indicated.

conditions.name: Acute urinary retention
conditions.opd: Assess painful inability to void, bladder distension, medications, neurological symptoms, infection and renal impairment.
conditions.indoor: Urgent decompression and monitoring per local protocol; assess urethral injury/stricture risk, renal function and cause; urgent urology review if catheterization fails or red flags exist.

conditions.name: Acute bacterial prostatitis
conditions.opd: Assess fever, pelvic/perineal pain, urinary symptoms, retention and sepsis. Avoid prostatic massage in suspected acute bacterial prostatitis.
conditions.indoor: Admit for sepsis, retention, inability to take oral therapy or severe illness; culture and treat according to local resistance guidance, with urology input if complications.

conditions.name: Conjunctivitis
conditions.opd: Assess vision, pain, photophobia, corneal involvement, contact lens use and neonatal status. Red eye with pain or reduced vision is not routine conjunctivitis.
conditions.indoor: Urgent ophthalmology review for visual loss, severe pain, corneal opacity, chemical injury, trauma or neonatal conjunctivitis.

conditions.name: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
conditions.opd: Severe painful red eye, blurred vision/haloes, headache, nausea or a fixed mid-dilated pupil requires immediate emergency ophthalmology referral.
conditions.indoor: Urgent pressure-lowering treatment and definitive ophthalmic intervention per specialist protocol; do not delay transfer.

conditions.name: Iron deficiency anaemia
conditions.opd: Confirm iron deficiency and investigate the cause (menstrual/GI blood loss, diet, pregnancy, malabsorption) rather than treating Hb alone.
conditions.indoor: Urgent stabilization for significant bleeding/instability; transfusion is not routine for stable iron deficiency. Arrange cause-specific treatment and follow-up response.

conditions.name: Fever of unknown source / acute fever
conditions.opd: Assess duration, travel/exposure, local epidemiology, vital signs, danger signs, pregnancy and immunocompromise; avoid indiscriminate antibiotics.
conditions.indoor: Admit/escalate for instability, altered consciousness, respiratory distress, severe dehydration, bleeding or organ dysfunction; test based on history and local epidemiology.
